collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A child asks an elder to tell the story of the great raid: tell it as a hero story, or tell it as it was.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every child on Isola knows there was a great raid long ago, and every child wants to hear about it. (friend) has asked (subject), who was there, to tell it. (subject) has a hero story ready, the one with the brave warriors and the clever trick with the fishing nets. (subject.He/she) also knows the parts nobody puts in hero stories. What should (subject) tell?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells the hero story, with the nets and the warriors and the raiders tumbling into the lagoon. (friend) is thrilled and acts it out for days. One day, (subject) thinks, (subject.he/she) will tell (friend.him/her) the rest.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tells the story as it was, gently: the nets and the courage, but also the fear, and the people who were missing afterwards. (friend) listens with big eyes. At the end, (friend.he/she) asks if it could happen again. (subject) says (subject.he/she) hopes not, and that is why everyone keeps watch.
